strengths: Principled and elegant mathematical framework: The paper systematically extends the orthogonal polynomial (OP) foundation of HiPPO to capture core capabilities of modern SSMs (nonlinear interaction, input-dependent selection, key-value associative recall, multiscale representation, and predictive state geometry) with mathematical rigor.

Superior mechanistic interpretability: By anchoring state updates and readouts in continuous-time OP theory, each mechanism exposes its internal workings in closed or directly visualizable forms—such as explicit Volterra kernels, dynamic history measures via time-warping (Eq. 5), reproducing kernel address spaces (Fig. 3 and 6), and predictive metric eigenfunctions (Fig. 5).

Thorough theoretical analyses in the appendices: Technical derivations, particularly the analysis in Appendix D.2 explaining why Jeffreys weighting fails to alter limiting Jacobi eigenvalue distributions due to the universal arcsine law and why the log-timescale formulation is required, provide substantial technical depth.

Intellectual honesty regarding empirical limitations: The authors explicitly evaluate and report results on character-level language modeling (WikiText-2), transparently discussing the trade-offs between interpretability and raw predictive performance, including the severe failure mode of continuous associative memory on autoregressive language modeling.
weaknesses: Evaluation is heavily reliant on idealized synthetic tasks: The primary validations (Wray & Green system, 30-step selective copying, 12-step associative recall, OU process reconstruction) are tailor-made to match the exact mathematical assumptions of each proposed variant. It remains unclear how robust these explicit mechanisms are under real-world noise, high-dimensional inputs, or misspecified dynamics.

Computational scalability barriers: Several variants introduce severe computational bottlenecks that contrast with the hardware-efficient linear scaling of modern SSMs (e.g., Volterra HiPPO scales as O(N^k), while the log-timescale multiscale update requires dense matrix operations scaling as O(NM^2) per step rather than fast parallel scans).

Disparate zoo rather than an integrated model: While the five extensions are conceptually unified under the HiPPO/OP umbrella, they remain isolated modules evaluated on distinct tasks. The work does not demonstrate whether or how these components can be composed into a coherent, multi-layer sequence model.

Underperformance on real-world data: On WikiText-2, all HiPPO variants trail standard baselines (LSTM, S4D, Mamba) by a noticeable margin (e.g., 6.80–7.52 test PPL vs. 5.54 for Mamba; 20.41 PPL for Associative Memory HiPPO), narrowing the immediate utility of these variants to niche diagnostic or scientific settings.

strengths: Principled and conceptually appealing framework: The paper provides a clean, mathematically grounded connection between classical approximation theory (orthogonal polynomials, Volterra series, reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces, spectral analysis) and the memory mechanisms utilized in modern sequence models.

Mechanistic interpretability: Unlike modern black-box state space models where selection and associative recall are buried in opaque recurrent or attention weights, the proposed zoo variants allow direct inspection and visualization of memory profiles, reproducing kernels, and predictive history geometries.

Theoretical depth in multiscale and forecasting extensions: The derivation of multiscale state representation using Jacobi matrices and the analysis of arcsine limiting spectral distributions (justifying the log-timescale parameterization) are mathematically sound and illuminating.

Intellectual honesty and transparency: The authors candidly present negative results and limitations, specifically documenting that the HiPPO zoo variants underperform Mamba and S4D on WikiText-2 character-level modeling and outlining clear computational trade-offs.
weaknesses: Fragmented formulation rather than a unified model: The paper presents five largely disconnected extensions ('zoo'), each evaluated on a bespoke synthetic toy task tailored to that specific mechanism, rather than demonstrating how these mechanisms can be composed into a coherent sequence modeling architecture.

Heavily synthetic and low-dimensional empirical evaluation: The synthetic tasks are small-scale (e.g., sequence lengths 12 to 30 for selective copying and associative recall; 1D Gaussian and OU processes). The only real-world benchmark (WikiText-2) shows severe degradation compared to standard baselines.

Scalability and parallelization bottlenecks: A major advantage of modern SSMs (S4, Mamba) is efficient parallel scanning or FFT convolutions during training. By introducing time-varying continuous modulation, dense scale couplings ($O(NM^2)$), or higher-order tensors ($O(N^k)$ for Volterra), several of these variants sacrifice the core computational efficiency that makes SSMs practical for long contexts.

Addressing mechanisms in Associative Memory HiPPO: Generating continuous scalar addresses via MLPs and using polynomial kernel projections for retrieval appears brittle and lacks scale-invariance, as reflected in its complete failure on autoregressive language modeling.

strengths: Principled and elegant mathematical framing: The manuscript nicely connects continuous-time orthogonal polynomial projections (HiPPO) with established classical concepts such as Volterra series, time-warping transformations, continuous reproducing kernels for associative memory, and spectral analysis of Jacobi matrices.

Theoretical insight in Multiscale HiPPO: The analysis in Appendix D.2 and D.3 is insightful, demonstrating via the Kuijlaars & Van Assche arcsine law why a simple compact measure reweighting on timescale parameter g fails to alter the asymptotic eigenvalue spectrum, which rigorously justifies the log-timescale formulation u = log g.

High interpretability and transparency: Unlike black-box neural SSMs, the proposed mechanisms allow direct functional inspection of memory contents, such as explicit 2D Volterra kernels (Figure 1), induced real-time weighting measures under salience (Figure 2), and continuous-time forecast-induced geometry (Figure 5).

Honest discussion of limitations: The authors commendably evaluate their models on natural language modeling (WikiText-2 in Appendix F and Section 3.6), openly reporting that the explicit formulations significantly lag behind modern SSMs like Mamba and S4D.
weaknesses: Fragmented collection of isolated vignettes: The 'HiPPO Zoo' introduces five separate, largely uncoupled mechanisms rather than a coherent, unified sequence modeling framework. It remains unclear how these mechanisms could be synthesized into a scalable general-purpose model.

Heavily contrived and small-scale synthetic evaluation: The synthetic tasks designed to validate each mechanism are minimal and artificial (e.g., selective copying sequences of length T = 30 in Section 3.2, and associative recall sequences of length T = 12 in Section 3.3). These toy setups do not demonstrate robust sequence modeling capabilities on non-trivial sequence lengths where SSMs typically shine.

Weak baselines on synthetic benchmarks: In Table 1, the baseline Transformer performs at chance (~22-33%) primarily because it is a single-layer model evaluated without positional encodings or adequate capacity on fixed length sequences. As Table 3 shows, simply adding positional embeddings and an extra layer allows the Transformer to reach 98.9%–99.7%, indicating that the synthetic advantage of Associative Memory HiPPO is overstated relative to standard architectures.

Loss of computational efficiency and parallelism: Modern SSMs (S4, Mamba, S5) derive their utility from fast parallel scans and structured low-rank or diagonal parameterizations. Several Zoo variants compromise this: Multiscale HiPPO introduces a dense matrix function G = exp(J) with O(NM^2) updates (Appendix D.3), Volterra HiPPO scales combinatorially as O(N^k), and the online updates in Associative Memory HiPPO require sequential step-by-step updates trained via truncated BPTT, forfeiting efficient convolution or parallel prefix scans.

Poor real-world performance: On the only real-world task evaluated (WikiText-2 character-level modeling, Table 4), all HiPPO Zoo variants trail far behind standard SSM and RNN baselines (e.g., Vanilla HiPPO + MLP achieves 6.80 PPL and Salience achieves 7.52 PPL vs. 5.54 for Mamba; Associative Memory HiPPO completely collapses at 20.41 PPL).
